title: Quiet ramp + backfill strategy (personal scratchpad)
content:
Context: quick personal notes for a lower-noise, low-latency rollout pattern that I want to test for the next model version. This is a scratchpad — rough ideas, heuristics, and experiment scaffolding. Goal is to reduce customer-observable volatility during rollouts while keeping ability to increase traffic quickly when signals look good.

High-level idea: 'Quiet ramp' = start with very small cohorts that exercise production routing, warm caches and KV, and verify stable p99 and correctness. Use a separate, short-lived backfill window to absorb request spikes without pushing new model to all users. Focus on: cohort selection (low-risk customers), short warm-up probes, conservative thresholds for promotion, automated backfill triggers and silent failure fallback.

Key constraints/assumptions:
- We have model variants: v2-quant (fast, slightly lower perf) and v2-std (higher perf). Both compatible with existing model API.
- Dedicated pool capacity limited in region-us-west1 during business hours.
- We can set per-client routing weights and holdouts via flag service (flag: model.v2.rollout.weight).
- Telemetry available: p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate (5xx), rejection-rate (503/429), token-cost delta, correctness check passrate (automated unit tests), hallucination proxy metric (eval set similarity).

Suggested ramp schedule (conservative):
- T0 (Day 0 morning): 0.1% global traffic -> 1000 requests or 30 minutes, whichever first. Cohort = small internal test orgs + 10 low-risk customer accounts.
- T1 (T0 + 4h): 0.5% global traffic -> 5k req or 2 hours. Add additional low-risk customers (beta program).
- T2 (T1 + 12h): 2% global -> 20k req or 6 hours. Open to more customers but still exclude high-frequency API keys.
- T3 (T2 + 24h): 10% global -> monitor for 24 hours, begin gradual split to 25% if stable.
- Fast path: if at any stage automated alarms green (p99 < SLO-10% and error < baseline +0.2%), we can accelerate doubling every X hours up to 25%.

Backfill window concept:
- Separate short-lived traffic buffer enabled at T2/T3 to allow short bursts to be served by fallback-capable hosts or by v2-quant, avoiding increasing global rollout weight.
- Backfill triggers: sudden surge > 3x baseline qps for >2m OR p99 increases > +40% without corresponding load increase.
- Backfill behavior: divert up to 5% of global traffic to a dedicated backfill pool with cached prefix reuse and higher concurrency. This pool runs v2-quant with extra KV caching margin.
- Backfill TTL: 10 minutes. Auto-evaluate every 5 minutes; drain when metrics return to baseline.

Version pinning and compatibility notes:
- Pinning: for customers with version pins (customer.metadata.request_pin = true), do NOT include in ramp cohorts unless they explicitly opt in. Maintain separate conversation store and KV mapping.
- Migration: if we detect client hardpins to v1, add a soft-redirect header in responses for debug, do not change routing.
- Rollback anchor: always keep v1 images in warm state for at least 30 minutes after switching traffic; this reduces cold-start induced latency for fast rollback.

Safety thresholds (proposal — conservative):
- Hard abort: any sustained 5xx > baseline +1.0% for 5 minutes OR p99 > SLO * 1.75 for 5 minutes.
- Soft hold: error +0.4% OR p99 > SLO*1.3 -> pause further ramp and revert to previous stable weight for 15 minutes.
- Cost check: token-cost delta > +30% over baseline for 1h -> pause ramp and investigate (quantization profile may be wrong).

Observability checklist (what I stare at):
- Global and per-region p50/p95/p99 latency charts, and sliding windows (1m/5m/1h)
- Error rates by type (5xx, 4xx), by client and by route
- Rejection rate and queue length on serving runtime workers
- Cache hit ratio for prefix/KV (new model should warm quicker if cache hit ratio high)
- Model output quality proxies: eval-check passrate, similarity-to-baseline on a small rolling prompt set
- Cost per 1k tokens (to flag regression) and token-distribution heatmap

Cohort selection heuristics (how to pick initial users):
- Internal orgs (always first) + a handful of opt-in customers from the beta list
- Prefer clients with low QPS, non-critical SLAs, and dedicated engineers willing to help debug
- Avoid high-volume transactional customers (payments, security scanners) until T3+

Runbook snippets (quick):
- Pause ramp: set model.v2.rollout.weight = model.v2.rollout.weight / 2 for 10m, then evaluate
- Full rollback: flip routing alias to v1-stable; keep rollback window open for 30m before re-evaluating
- Enable backfill manually: set flag traffic.backfill.enabled=true and traffic.backfill.weight=5; monitor

Questions / unknowns I want to answer before next run:
- How fast can the backfill pool be provisioned under heavy load? (SREs: what is typical cold-start time?)
- Do we have a simple way to compute token-cost delta per request in near-real-time? (billing infra)
- Are there customers with soft-pins that will be silently broken by minor output formatting changes? Need list.

Immediate TODOs (for next 48h):
- Sync with SRE on backfill pool warmup times (Ravi)

notes: This is intentionally conservative — want to avoid noisy rollouts that trigger support tickets.
Prefer conservative cost gates early; can open faster if quality signals are strong.
Keep an eye on rare tokens that increase compute by small fraction but huge cost over time.
